Frame-by-frame

Build prompt

Rebuild this interaction 1:1: Must's review sheet - a bottom sheet for rating a movie where a horizontal 1-10 number row slides under a fixed emoji that reacts to the value (dead face at 1, neutral mid, heart-eyes at 10), ending in a Save button.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Bottom sheet over a dimmed movie detail (Oppenheimer). Sheet: movie row (thumbnail, title, date), a "Write your review..." field, a rating strip - a gray gear icon, a blue circle showing the current value, numbers 10..1 across, with a reactive emoji at the left end - and a full-width blue "Save" button.

## Motion spec
Pattern: reactive emoji rating scrubber.
- Sheet entry: rises (spring ~320/24), backdrop dims 50%; the rating strip is pre-filled at 10.
- Scrub the numbers: the row slides horizontally 1:1 under the fixed blue indicator circle; the value in the circle rolls (digit animation, 150ms) as it passes each number, with a light haptic tick per integer.
- The emoji reacts per range: 1-2 a green queasy face, 3-4 a weary face, 5-6 neutral, 7-8 a slight smile, 9 a big grin, 10 heart-eyes - each swap is a 250ms crossfade with a small pop (scale 1.2 -> 1, spring ~460/18).
- Velocity on release carries the row with momentum, decelerating to the nearest integer (spring ~300/22 snap).
- Save: the button dips (scale 0.97, 120ms), the sheet drops away, and the rating appears on the detail page behind (fade in, 250ms).

## Calibration
- The indicator circle stays centered; the numbers move - never the reverse.
- Emoji changes only on settled values, not mid-scrub flicker (100ms debounce).

## Reduced motion
Sheet fades; numbers snap without momentum.

## Don't miss
- The emoji is the emotional readout - it must be big enough to read at a glance and visibly change across the range.
- 10 is preselected: the flow assumes enthusiasm and lets the user dial down.
